openingExtrasRules.notes: The dealer confirmed on 2026-09-11 that a Mahogany Contemporary unit ships prehung with its jamb, so the jamb legs are not sold beside it, and neither are the glass bead, the subsills, the loose casings and brick mould, the mull covers, the astragals or the mullion. The collection is not offered with simulated divided lites at all. The construction-door adder is the one component that remains. Jamb DEPTH is still asked: the unit is built to a wall thickness and the order sheet has to carry it.

trimProfileRules.label: Interior casing profile
trimProfileRules.note: which casing goes on the inside face
trimProfileRules.notes: The prehang adder prices casing an opening once whatever the profile. The dealer confirmed on 2026-09-11 that the wider 3-1/2" profile costs the difference between the two casing rows on top — $17.00 on both wood lines today. Derived from the rows rather than stored, so a vendor reprice carries through.

trimProfileRules.label: Exterior trim profile

trimProfileRules.notes: Both profiles are priced identically on both wood lines ($45.00 mahogany, $52.00 knotty alder), so the choice is a specification and costs nothing today. The difference is still computed rather than assumed to be zero, so a reprice would be picked up.

dentilShelfRule.label: Dentil shelf
dentilShelfRule.notes: Mahogany catalog pages 18-19 print two part numbers for each Craftsman size, Shelf Yes and Shelf No, and the Dealer Wood Pricing sheet prices one row per size — so on a wood door the shelf costs nothing and only changes the number. The $184.00 dentil shelf in the catalogue is a FIBERGLASS component and is not charged here; no shelf appears anywhere on the seven pages of the wood sheet. MCM--3068S already carries the S: the sheet prices only that variant at 6'8", so it is not asked. Confirmed with the dealer 2026-09-11.

speakeasyOptions.notes: The catalog prints "*Speakeasy kits & iron mask options available" beside nine doors and the price sheet then prices every combination as its own part number. The number is the plain door's with SE, a mask code and an insert code spliced in front of the size code: KA2PSQ + SE + B + W + 3068. Reading that grammar means a door Hoelscher adds to the programme appears on its own, with no code change here. A door offers the programme when at least one such part number is priced. Four rows carry a misprinted part number; skuCorrections says where each belongs and what to tell the customer.
speakeasyOptions.insertNote: Hoelscher prices the kit the same with a wood or a glass insert.
speakeasyOptions.unpricedNote: Hoelscher prints no price for this combination — ask the factory.

notMade.reason: The Balfour pattern does not fit a circle-top door. Confirmed by the dealer 2026-09-10, which is why the sheet prices no such row.

hiddenVariants.notes: The fiberglass 2 Panel Arch names its speakeasy variants in words rather than in the part number and prices the masked ones as CONFIGURED ITEM with no part number at all. The dealer does not sell fiberglass speakeasy doors (confirmed 2026-09-10), so these rows stay in the catalogue for reference but are not shown as cards to quote from.

prehangAdderRules.notes: A prehang adder is not something a customer picks off a list: which row applies is decided by the door they already chose. The sheet keys each row by line, top style and a configuration string that carries the size and the opening. Square-top rows spell the opening out; arch- and circle-top rows are keyed by size alone, because the vendor prices one trim per size whatever the opening. The app reads that here rather than carrying it in code.
prehangAdderRules.slabNote: A slab is not hung, so it takes no prehang adder.

sdlRule.notes: Hoelscher applies simulated divided lites at the factory and bills per lite, so the count is a question on the door rather than bar stock off a shelf. The Dealer Wood Pricing sheet prices it +35 per lite with the 7/8" bar and +40 with the 1-1/4", so the bar is asked. Mahogany catalog page 21 offers the grid on one door, the 3/4 Lite 1 Panel for SDL, so on wood it is offered there and nowhere else; the lineal bars in the components sections remain, for a grid applied in-house. Confirmed by the dealer 2026-09-10 and 2026-09-12.

skuPlaceholders.notes: A part number on the price sheet can carry more than one placeholder. The first is always the glass code (see glassCodes). A trailing one, or the one after a decorative-glass design infix, is filled at order time from something the configurator already knows. Only patterns confirmed against a real catalog page are listed here — anything else is flagged on the order sheet rather than guessed at.

handing.evidence: Catalog page 10-11 lists the numbers in full: M3GPWNSR2880L and M3GPWNSR2880R for the two handings of the 2'8" x 8'0", and likewise for 3'0" x 8'0". The glass code sits in the first placeholder, the handing letter in the trailing one.

caming.evidence: Catalog page 25 lists the numbers in full beside the caming: MCABLAP3068 Patina, MCABLAZ3068 Zinc. The placeholder after the design infix BLA is the caming letter, not a glass code.
